You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | U.S. New Tariffs Take Effect Amid Rising Middle East Risks; Intel Beats Expectations as AI Competition Shifts; Magnificent Seven All Fall, Tesla Plunges Hard (July 24, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics Surging oil prices push up rate-hike expectations; market prices in roughly 36% probability of a hike next week.
Escalating Middle East conflict drove Brent crude above $100. The 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.365%, while 10-year and 30-year yields also hit fresh year-to-date highs.
CME FedWatch shows the probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike next week near 36%. Market impact: Rising inflation concerns pressure short-end rate-sensitive assets. The dollar and U.S. Treasury yields move higher in tandem, significantly reducing risk appetite.
International Commodities U.S. new tariffs take effect today; Middle East risks lift oil prices.
New import tariffs took effect at 00:01 ET Friday, with rates of 10%–12.5% covering about 60 economies. Mexico, the UK, Canada, and India face 10%; the EU at least 10%; Japan, South Korea, and Switzerland at least 12.5%.
Saudi oil tanker attacks and escalating U.S.-Iran tensions pushed Brent briefly above $100. Market impact: Higher trade costs combined with geopolitical risk premium temporarily support energy prices and reinforce inflation expectations, benefiting some safe-haven assets while suppressing risk appetite.
U.S.-Iran Developments Middle East conflict escalates; U.S. threatens large-scale action.
Trump said he is seriously considering restarting large-scale military operations against Iran and warned that Houthi attacks will be attributed to Iran. Both Iran and the Houthis stated they are prepared to respond.
Israel’s Defense Minister also indicated readiness. Market impact: Geopolitical risk premium directly lifts oil prices and safe-haven demand, while the inflation channel raises rate-hike expectations, amplifying overall market volatility.
II. Market Recap
Commodities & FX Performance
Spot gold : ~$4,050/oz, +0.02%
Spot silver : ~$57.75/oz, +0.17%
WTI crude: ~$92.14/bbl, –0.05%
Brent crude: ~$87/bbl, +0.1%
U.S. Dollar Index (DXY): 101.426, –0.02
Driver analysis: Escalating Middle East conflict and attacks on Saudi tankers directly pushed oil higher. Combined with the implementation of new U.S. tariffs, trade-cost concerns intensified and inflation expectations rose clearly. Gold and silver received support as safe-haven assets, but a stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields exerted pressure. Institutions believe short-term commodities remain driven by the dual forces of geopolitics and policy. High energy prices may prolong the Fed’s tightening expectations. The inter-asset linkage shows the chain: higher oil → inflation concerns → higher rates → pressure on risk assets.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$65,000, –1.82%
ETH : ~$1,870, –3.35%
Total crypto market cap: $2.31 trillion, –1.1%
Liquidations: 24h total $252 million, of which long liquidations $189 million
Bitget BTC/ USDT liquidation map: Current price ~$64,829. Large clusters of short liquidations sit above at $65,500–$66,500. A continued upward move could trigger concentrated short covering and accelerate the rally. Long liquidations are mainly concentrated in the $64,000–$63,500 zone, but the overall size is smaller than above, so the short-term liquidation structure still favor s sweeping short liquidity first.
Spot ETF net flows: Yesterday net inflow $69 million; current 24h dynamic net outflow $23 million.
Driver analysis: Declining risk appetite in U.S. equities and oil-driven higher rate-hike expectations exerted macro pressure on crypto. ETF flows show cautious institutional stance; leverage liquidations reflect sensitive sen time nt. BTC held key ranges relatively well, while ETH showed weaker elasticity. Institutional consensus points to short-term sideways-to-weak action; focus remains on Fed policy signals and geopolitical developments transmitting to risk assets.
U.S. Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones: Closed 51,711.65, –0.97%
S&P 500: Closed 7,408.30, –1.21%
Nasdaq : Closed 25,137.69, –2.15%; tech and growth stocks under clear pressure
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : 208.76 (–1.56%)
AAPL : 321.66 (–1.30%)
MSFT : 381.58 (–2.24%)
GOOGL : 317.69 (–7.13%)
AMZN : 233.66 (–4.57%)
META : 606.10 (–3.36%)
TSLA : 319.69 (–14.52%)
Performance summary & driver analysis: The Magnificent Seven all declined. Tesla plunged after Q2 profits fell far short of expectations. Google dropped sharply after raising full-year capex guidance to as high as $205 billion, sparking AI spending concerns. Middle East conflict-driven oil prices and higher rate-hike expectations jointly suppressed risk appetite. Stock performance diverged significantly: memory stocks rose against the market, while high-valuation growth names came under heavier pressure, showing the market shifting from “AI narrative” toward “return validation” and macro risk pricing.
Sector Moves
Memory concept rose against the market
Representative stocks: Micron +3.2%, SK Hynix +2.56%.
[...]
Drivers: Google’s increased AI spending benefits high-bandwidth memory demand; capital flowed back into tight-supply segments amid the broader pullback.
[...]
1. Intel ( INTC ) – Q2 Results Far Exceed Expectations Event overview: Intel Q2 revenue $16.13 billion, +25% YoY (est. $14.43 billion); Data Center & AI revenue $6.26 billion (est. $5.54 billion); adjusted EPS $0.42 (est. $0.21). Q3 guidance: revenue $15.8–16.8 billion, adjusted EPS $0.38, both above consensus. Management noted strong double-digit growth in server CPUs and said 2027 capex will be significantly higher than 2026. Market interpretation: Institutions view this as one of the strongest growth periods in 15 years, clearly validating AI demand and reshaping Intel’s competitive position in data-center and AI chips. Analysts are watching the competitive landscape versus AMD and Nvidia as well as the long-term capex trajectory. Investment implication: Beat-and-raise results provide medium-term support; monitor subsequent execution and market-share changes.
[...]
2. Tesla (TSLA) – Earnings Miss Triggers Sharp Sell-Off Event overview: Tesla Q2 profits far below expectations; shares plunged ~14%–15% in a single day. Shorts booked ~$4.12 billion in gains that day. Tesla has the highest short interest among the Magnificent Seven (~3% of float). BNP Paribas maintains a Sell rating and $280 target , noting the valuation already embeds very high AI expectations. Market interpretation: Institutions remain cautious on aggressive capex and the pace of AI progress. Deliveries were strong, but profit quality and Robotaxi commercialization remain key variables. Retail added on the dip, while institutions focus more on return validation. Investment implication: Short-term volatility is amplified; track actual contributions from AI and energy businesses plus any full-year guidance revisions.
[...]
3. Google (GOOGL) – Strong Cloud Business but Capex Hike Sparks Concerns Event overview: Google Cloud CEO said existing customers are spending ~50% more than committed amounts, driving rapid cloud growth. However, the company raised full-year capex guidance to as high as $205 billion, causing shares to drop more than 7% intraday. Market interpretation: Institutions acknowledge cloud differentiation and execution strength but growing concern over the return timeline of continuously expanding AI investment. Analysts focus on search-ad resilience and capex efficiency. Investment implication: Long-term positive for cloud and AI ecosystem, but near-term validation of revenue conversion from heavy investment is needed.
